papers.title: KinaseDB: an integrated multi-omics platform for the human kinome with disease-specific target prioritization.
papers.summary: KinaseDB is a web platform integrating multi-omics data for 559 human protein kinases from 11 resources, including structures, druggability, kinase-substrate relationships, single-cell expression across 625 tissue-cell-type combinations, disease associations, and population genetic variation. Its kinase prioritization score spans 69 disease contexts and separated approved kinase-inhibitor targets from dark kinases with AUROC 0.773; all data and a REST API are public.

papers.title: Analog neural network-based wireless receiver.
papers.summary: The authors built an analog wireless receiver that uses neural network principles, implemented with memristor crossbar arrays on a system-on-a-chip, to perform channel equalization, filtering, routing, and symbol detection without a mixer. The hardware achieved a bit error rate of 10^-6 across modulation schemes and carrier frequencies, with favorable energy efficiency and speed versus digital AI implementations.

papers.title: Herpesviruses hijack ISGylation to promote viral capsid assembly.
papers.summary: Using murine gammaherpesvirus 68, the authors show ISGylation is hijacked to promote lytic replication: co-infection with oral bacterium Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans boosted ISG15 expression, and viral structural proteins were dominant ISGylation targets. ISGylation of major capsid protein ORF25 was required for efficient capsid assembly and virion maturation across herpesviruses, revealing how microbes can amplify viral infection via an innate immune effector.

papers.title: Mapping structural constraints and adaptive potential in a capsule-degrading phage tailspike protein.
papers.summary: Deep mutational scanning of the E. coli K1 phage K1F endosialidase tailspike generated 22,365 single-amino-acid variants. The tailspike is structurally fragile but contains adaptive pockets: active-site mutations accommodate longer sialic acid chains, beta-helix stalk mutations tune processivity and specificity, and host-range discrimination maps to beta-barrel loops and distal residues, informing design of phages that defeat capsule-based bacterial defenses.

papers.title: Mutant p53 sensitizes KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma to immunotherapy by repressing SPP1.
papers.summary: KRAS/TP53 co-mutation predicts favorable immune checkpoint blockade response in lung adenocarcinoma. Mutant p53 synergizes with FOXA1 to repress SPP1 transcription while KRAS upregulates SPP1 via MAPK-ERK-STAT1 signaling. Low SPP1 reduces myeloid-derived suppressor cell recruitment and increases CD8+ T cell infiltration; SPP1 blockade synergized with anti-PD-1 therapy in KRAS-mutant xenograft models.

papers.title: Targeting tumor-associated macrophages using mRNA lipid nanoparticles for cytotoxic T lymphocyte-mediated cancer immunotherapy.
papers.summary: An antibody-coated lipid nanoparticle targeting TREM2 on tumor-associated macrophages co-delivers a toll-like receptor agonist and CXCL9-encoding mRNA. In preclinical models this reprogrammed the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, improved cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration and activity, and combined with anti-PD-L1/anti-CTLA-4 promoted durable memory immunity, offering a targeted mRNA-nanoparticle approach to cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Transgenerational chromosome repair in the asexual bdelloid rotifer Adineta vaga.
papers.summary: The asexual bdelloid rotifer Adineta vaga uses homologous recombination both for oogenesis-like crossovers and gene conversion and for genome repair after DNA damage. The authors propose break-induced homologous extension repair (BIHER), in which broken chromosomes are progressively restored across multiple generations, potentially a key adaptation of asexual life in extreme environments.

papers.title: Kappa opioids suppress histaminergic itch by inhibiting mediodorsal thalamus-projecting claustrum glutamatergic neurons.
papers.summary: Glutamatergic claustrum neurons projecting to the mediodorsal thalamus promote histamine-induced scratching in mice: chemogenetic inhibition reduced scratching, activation increased it. These neurons highly express kappa opioid receptors, and nalfurafine's antipruritic effect depends on KOR in claustrum neurons and the claustrum-thalamus circuit, clarifying how kappa opioids suppress histaminergic itch.

papers.title: Diverse ancestral myosin motors generate and segregate distinct types of nanocluster-rich domains at the plasma membrane.
papers.summary: Two classes of ancestral nonmuscle myosins organize plasma membrane domains: class I myosins link GPI-anchored outer-leaflet molecules to actin, while class II myosins act on transmembrane proteins with actin-binding capacity. Consistent with active Flory-Huggins phase separation, these motors generate spatially segregated nanocluster-rich mesoscale domains, providing an ATP-driven mechanism for membrane organization and signaling.

papers.title: Acetyl-CoA-dependent processes are preferentially supported by local metabolite synthesis.
papers.summary: Using cell lines with ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) restricted to nucleus or cytosol, the authors show either pool supports fatty acid synthesis and histone acetylation, but local synthesis gives finer control: nuclear ACLY preserves histone H3K23 acetylation under glucose limitation and shapes specific transcriptional programs, while cytosolic ACLY best supports lipid biosynthetic flux.

papers.title: Robust cellular transformations of PET deconstruction products by import of glycol esters.
papers.summary: Terephthalic acid (TPA) uptake limits cellular valorization of PET deconstruction products. The authors found that glycol ester products MHET and BHET are imported rapidly and pH-independently in E. coli lacking a TPA transporter. Exploiting this plus oxidoreductase deletions enabled intracellular hydrolysis routes, yielding upcycled reduction products from BHET and real PET waste at >90% and >80% yields.

papers.title: Elucidating the role of DEAF1 in neurodevelopment and shared molecular pathways in high-risk autism genes using cortical organoids.
papers.summary: A DEAF1 mutation in human embryonic stem cells disrupts chromatin accessibility at neuronal gene loci; in cortical organoids it causes aberrant progenitor proliferation, disrupted lamination, and impaired neuronal differentiation. WNT, TGF-beta, and cell-cycle pathways are shared dysregulated hubs across autism-risk genes, and a porcupine inhibitor partially rescues DEAF1-mutant organoid phenotypes, supporting pathway-targeted therapy.

papers.title: AT1R-mediated NIR-II/PA imaging-guided iCM exosome therapy for myocardial ischemia revascularization.
papers.summary: A theranostic platform combines a dual NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic imaging probe targeting angiotensin II type 1 receptor with losartan and exosomes from induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. In mouse and rat ischemia-reperfusion models, imaging-guided delivery enhanced angiogenesis, reduced fibrosis, and improved cardiac recovery, integrating diagnosis and spatially precise therapy for myocardial injury.

papers.title: Ex vivo bone marrow subniches influence the fate of human antibody-secreting cells.
papers.summary: A perfusable human bone marrow-on-a-chip with endosteal and perivascular niches was used to study human antibody-secreting cells (ASCs). ASCs migrated through vessels, clustered perivascularly near survival factors, and the endosteal niche strongly affected survival and retention. A subset showed CXCR4-CXCL12-regulated stop-and-go migration, defining how human marrow subniches cooperatively regulate plasma cell fate.

papers.title: RNA-independent cis-autoregulatory circuits within bidirectional gene pairs control metabolism.
papers.summary: In bidirectional lncRNA/protein-coding gene pairs in liver, lncRNA transcription cis-activates the coding gene via an active promoter-proximal enhancer, while coding-gene transcription reciprocally cis-inhibits the lncRNA. Both directions are RNA-independent, driven by the transcription process. Blocking lncRNA transcription in vivo reduced the partner gene and induced hepatic steatosis, showing metabolic importance of these autoregulatory circuits.

papers.title: The FAP × CD3 bispecific antibody OMTX305 induces T cell-mediated antitumor effects in patient-derived ex vivo models of solid tumors.
papers.summary: OMTX305 is a bispecific trivalent T cell engager targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP) on cancer-associated fibroblasts and CD3. In patient-derived lung and ovarian tumor slices co-cultured with autologous PBMCs, it eliminated FAP+ fibroblasts, induced interferon responses and matrix remodeling, and triggered bystander tumor cell killing; immune phenotypes and PD-L1 patterns may stratify responders.

papers.title: The CENP-A chaperone complex spatially organizes centromeres.
papers.summary: In interphase, CENP-A and the constitutive centromere-associated network form shell-like structures enclosing a chromatin-poor cavity occupied by the CENP-A chaperone complex. Chaperone presence, but not its CENP-loading activity, is required for shell architecture; CENP-C scaffolding recruits the HJURP chaperone. The chaperone machinery thus structurally organizes centromeres independently of new CENP-A deposition.

papers.title: Learning stochastic dynamics and cell-fate landscapes from single-cell snapshots via optimal transport.
papers.summary: DiffusionOT is a machine learning framework that infers cell-state transition dynamics from multi-timepoint single-cell RNA-seq snapshots by learning stochastic forces via optimal transport and neural networks. It includes lineage tracing and in silico gene perturbation modules, and benchmarks on simulated and four real datasets, including spatial stereo-seq data, show accurate recovery of trajectories, growth, and cell-fate landscapes.

papers.title: TCR-JANUS engager proteins enable bispecific targeting to overcome tumor heterogeneity in TCR-T cell therapy.
papers.summary: TCR-JANUS engagers bind the variable region of a transgenic TCR and a tumor surface antigen, unlike CD3-targeting engagers. Combined with KRAS-G12V-specific TCR-T cells, a TCR-JANUS targeting TROP2 enabled dual-antigen recognition, suppressing antigenically heterogeneous tumors while preserving cognate specificity and reducing T cell exhaustion versus anti-CD3 engagers under chronic stimulation.

papers.title: Early detection of invasive lung cancer and multiorgan metastasis by a collagen-targeted protein MRI contrast agent.
papers.summary: LKB1/STK11-inactivated lung adenocarcinoma upregulates collagen I via focal adhesion kinase. The authors developed hProCA32.collagen, a collagen I-targeted MRI contrast agent with 10-fold higher relaxivity than clinical gadolinium agents. It enabled early, noninvasive MRI detection and quantification of lung tumors and metastases, including adrenal lesions, outperforming CT and standard MRI without radiation.

papers.title: A direct protein bridge connects the ds and ds-ss junction telomeric DNA segments in C. elegans.
papers.summary: Combining crystallography with in vivo analysis in C. elegans, the authors show the OB domain of POT-1 is repurposed to bind TEBP-1/2, forming a three-way TEBP-1/2-POT-1-DNA junction complex at telomeres. Disrupting these electrostatic interfaces disassembles the complex and causes telomere hyperelongation, defining how a simplified telomere proteome maintains chromosome-end homeostasis.

papers.title: Rubisco functional integrity requires a dedicated three-step maturation pathway.
papers.summary: Rubisco's catalytic subunit RbcL undergoes atypical N-terminal maturation: initiator methionine-serine cleavage followed by proline acetylation. The authors define a dedicated pathway of two aminopeptidases and an N-acetyltransferase that executes this, coupled to chaperone-assisted assembly; disruption reduces Rubisco accumulation, activase-mediated activation, and stability during senescence.

papers.title: Astrocytes mediate the dopaminergic modulation of tonic GABAergic signaling in substantia nigra.
papers.summary: In mouse midbrain slices, D2 dopamine receptor signaling suppresses tonic GABA(A)-mediated inhibition of substantia nigra reticulata neurons. This disinhibition required D2R-expressing astrocytes and GAT-3-mediated GABA uptake, while the source GABA derives from ALDH1A1+ dopaminergic neurons via GAT-1, demonstrating that astrocytes mediate dopaminergic control of nigral circuits and motor behavior.

papers.title: Metabolic regulation of calcium homeostasis via SERCA succination.
papers.summary: Fumarate suppresses SERCA calcium pump activity by succinating a conserved cysteine (Cys875 in SERCA2B), impairing ER calcium uptake. A succination-resistant Cys875Ser knock-in in flies preserved ER calcium homeostasis and protected against hyperglycemia and reduced survival on high-sugar diet, linking glucose metabolism to calcium homeostasis through a specific metabolite-protein modification.

papers.title: A systematic comparison of single-cell perturbation response prediction models.
papers.summary: A benchmark of 13 single-cell perturbation-response prediction methods across 25 datasets evaluated unseen perturbations, combinatorial effects, and cell-type transfer using 24 metrics. Performance depended strongly on effect size and metric choice; models showed conservative bias, PerturbNet best recovered differential-expression signatures, and no method generalized across cell types, establishing current limits for virtual-cell modeling.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal mapping of tertiary lymphoid structure heterogeneity shapes immune niches and clinical outcomes in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.summary: A multimodal spatial atlas of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma identified intratumoral TLSs as independent prognostic markers. Proteomics defined a four-tier TLS-based tumor microenvironment classification and a random forest predictor; imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics resolved TLS niches, maturation stages, and CAF-macrophage communication, informing stroma-directed immunotherapy.

papers.title: BCL11B predetermines a persister state in breast cancer that is reversed by TNFα.
papers.summary: Single-cell atlases identify an immature basal-like breast cancer cell population marked by BCL11B whose abundance correlates with early relapse after chemotherapy. BCL11B delineates a state that preferentially transitions to drug-resistant persister cells, and TNF-alpha acts as a natural BCL11B inhibitor that can reverse persister emergence, nominating BCL11B as a predictive marker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Substrate heterogeneity promotes cancer cell dissemination through interface roughening.
papers.summary: Using microengineered environments with tunable geometry, the authors show that spatial disorder of obstacles, more than obstacle presence, shifts cancer cell invasion from collective to single-cell dissemination, comparable in strength to loss of cell-cell adhesion. Live imaging and minimal biophysical modeling identify universality classes of invasion dynamics governed by environmental geometry.

papers.title: Mechanistic trade-offs between local and long-range signaling activity in natural and synthetic morphogens.
papers.summary: Hedgehog morphogens are dual-lipid modified yet form long-range gradients. Single-molecule tracking and synthetic ligands show palmitate directly promotes receptor engagement, whereas cholesterol confines secreted morphogen on the cell surface, acting as a nonsignaling co-receptor that enriches ligand locally at the cost of long-range diffusion, revealing an intrinsic trade-off between signaling potency and gradient formation.

papers.title: Rhomboid protease Rhbdl2 influences macrophage recruitment and wound repair in zebrafish.
papers.summary: CRISPR-Cas9 rhomboid protease Rhbdl2 mutants in zebrafish show enhanced wound repair with faster macrophage migration and accumulation at wounds, elevated apoptosis and proliferation. Proteomics revealed increased Rac2, and Rac2 knockdown suppressed the phenotype, identifying Rhbdl2 as a restraint on macrophage recruitment during tissue repair with implications for inflammation, fibrosis, and tumor immunity.

papers.title: Early glucagon-positive cells restrict pancreatic branching through VMAT2-noradrenaline-mediated ROS signaling.
papers.summary: In pancreatic bud explants, vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) in early glucagon/insulin co-expressing cells limits branching morphogenesis. Inhibiting VMAT2-mediated catecholamine uptake or noradrenaline synthesis/transport increased branching and insulin-positive cells via reduced ROS signaling; VMAT2 deletion in glucagon+ cells increased branching and islet area, linking monoamine-ROS signaling to pancreas development.

papers.title: Nutrient deprivation enhances the cytotoxic effects of a sulfonamide-chalcone hybrid in PC-3 prostate cancer cells.
papers.summary: The sulfonamide-chalcone hybrid SSC185 reduced PC-3 prostate cancer cell viability concentration- and time-dependently (IC50 24.7 uM at 24 h), with markedly enhanced potency under serum deprivation (IC50 4.2 uM). Mechanistically it raised SQSTM1/p62 and LC3B-I without LC3B-II conversion or acidic vesicle formation, reduced AKT/RPS6 signaling, and caused mitochondrial dysfunction, linking autophagy inhibition and nutrient context to cytotoxicity.

papers.title: Mitochondria-mediated anticancer effects of two previously characterized COX-2 inhibitors in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.summary: Two previously characterized COX-2 inhibitors, ZMA-M3 and ZMA-M4, showed selective cytotoxicity toward isolated hepatocellular carcinoma cells versus normal rat hepatocytes. They induced apoptosis (Annexin V/PI, caspase-3 activation) with mitochondrial ROS generation, membrane potential collapse, swelling, and cytochrome c release, supporting mitochondria-mediated apoptosis as their anticancer mechanism in HCC.

papers.title: Elucidation of the Biosynthesis of Pantocin A.
papers.summary: Pantocin A is a RiPP antibiotic inhibiting histidine biosynthesis. The authors resolve the structure of the PaaA product, clarifying prior ambiguity, and show PaaB is an Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent enzyme that accepts this substrate and catalyzes a unique 1,4-dehydrogenation to install the mature post-translational modification, completing the pantocin A biosynthetic pathway.

papers.title: Estimating cis and trans contributions to differences in gene regulation.
papers.summary: The authors present a coordinate system and hypothesis-testing framework for assigning cis versus trans regulation to gene expression differences between homozygous strains or species. Application to yeast, human-chimpanzee hybrid cells, and mouse data with replicates yields assignments that differ markedly from prior reports, and the framework models context dependency and mechanistic hypotheses for trans effects.

papers.title: Genetic control of a multifunctional trait: The central role of a fatty acid synthase gene in regulating survival and sexual communication.
papers.summary: In the parasitoid wasp Nasonia vitripennis, the fatty acid synthase gene fas3 underlies cuticular hydrocarbons serving dual functions: knockdown decreases desiccation-stress survival and completely depletes female sexual attractiveness, functioning as pheromone. fas3 is co-expressed with other CHC biosynthesis genes and shows sex-specific developmental expression, illuminating genetic control of a multifunctional trait.

papers.title: Signals of Natural Selection Across Regions of Low Recombination in Wild Populations of the Purple Sea Urchin, Strongylocentrotus purpuratus.
papers.summary: Whole-genome analysis of 137 purple sea urchins across seven populations identified nine low-recombination regions with signatures consistent with chromosomal inversions, three showing balancing and spatially heterogeneous selection with allelic-age patterns and enrichment for biomineralization and development genes. These are the first such regions reported in this species, linking structural variation to local adaptation.

papers.title: Weak but repeated patterns of co-introgression of nuclear OXPHOS genes and mitochondrial DNA in Iberian wall lizards.
papers.summary: In Iberian Podarcis wall lizards, where four mitochondrial introgression events are now documented, capture-sequencing of nuclear OXPHOS genes revealed weak but consistently significant partial co-introgression of nucoxphos genes with mitochondrial DNA in three of four cases, including introgression from an extinct ghost lineage, supporting co-transfer as a response to mitonuclear incompatibilities.

papers.title: Transcriptomic signatures of carotenoid-based color polytypism in Oophaga granulifera (Anura: Dendrobatidae).
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Comparing red aposematic and green cryptic Oophaga granulifera frogs, red skin accumulates keto-carotenoids, xanthophylls, and beta-carotene, with differential expression of carotenoid metabolism genes; bco1 is upregulated in green frogs and ttc39b in red livers. Red frogs also upregulate amino acid, lipid, and mitochondrial energy metabolism, suggesting keto-carotenoid accumulation links to higher metabolic rate.

papers.title: CaMKIIβ Signaling drives expression of metabolic and stress response genes in skeletal muscle, and its loss contributes to the LGMDR1 phenotype.
papers.summary: Muscle-specific Camk2b knockout mice develop myopathy, weakness, impaired oxidative-metabolism and stress-response gene upregulation after exercise, and reduced mitochondrial complex I/II and fatty acid oxidation activity, mirroring LGMDR1 patient biopsies. Constitutively active CaMKII-beta overexpression in Calpain 3 knockout muscle improved oxidative metabolism and function, supporting CaMKII-beta signaling as a therapeutic target in LGMDR1.

papers.title: Developmental regulation of progenitor aging shapes long-term intestinal homeostasis in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Genetic modulation of aging pathways in Drosophila larval adult midgut progenitors determines adult intestinal homeostasis: inducing aging-associated programs causes aberrant proliferation, skewed differentiation, barrier dysfunction, genomic instability, and destabilized islet architecture, whereas reversing them leaves the barrier intact, establishing developmental progenitor aging as a determinant of long-term tissue homeostasis.

papers.title: GenBank mining reveals novel insights into Rhizobium phylogeny: Identical 16S rRNA sequences are mainly uncoupled from species designation, host plant, and geographic origin: How this search suggested the definition of a direct 'microbial h-index'.
papers.summary: Analysis of 6,660 GenBank Rhizobium 16S rRNA sequences with 116,069 pairwise matches shows 66.6% of identical sequence pairs are fully discordant for species name, host plant, and country, and only 1.4% share all three. 16S identity is thus largely uncoupled from metadata, challenging fine-scale taxonomic inference and supporting polyphasic taxonomy; the authors propose a 'microbial h-index' for sequence reuse.

papers.title: Identification of functional genes and immune cell infiltration analysis in liposarcoma.
papers.summary: Bioinformatic analysis of liposarcoma identified differentially expressed hub genes, with high TYMS, KIF20A, BUB1B, LMNB1, RRM2, ZWINT, and RACGAP1 associated with poor overall and disease-free survival. RT-qPCR validated expression findings, and CIBERSORT showed higher resting mast cell fractions in tumors, nominating potential diagnostic biomarkers and immune-infiltration features for liposarcoma.

papers.title: 4D-DIA proteomics reveals distinct proteolytic landscapes induced by mechanical stress, Agrobacterium, and a viral capsid precursor.
papers.summary: High-depth 4D-DIA proteomics in Nicotiana benthamiana disentangled host responses to mechanical infiltration, Agrobacterium, and recombinant cargo (GFP vs FMDV capsid precursor P1-2A). Buffer infiltration independently induced cell-wall remodeling and oxidative stress; a core Agrobacterium-responsive proteome showed a growth-defense trade-off; P1-2A upregulated subtilases and cysteine proteases, informing plant molecular farming design.

papers.title: Differential effects of BCG-Russia and BCG-TICE on trained immunity: Potential implications for bladder cancer immunotherapy.
papers.summary: Comparing intravenous BCG-Russia versus BCG-TICE in mice, BCG-TICE elicited stronger trained immunity four weeks later, with higher proinflammatory cytokine production upon secondary activation, upregulated inflammation-related genes, and enriched functional pathways, while both strains expanded hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Strain-dependent innate memory differences may affect non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: A dual role of AcSDKP in chronic kidney disease: Targeting pericyte-driven fibrosis and vascular repair via VEGF/FGFR1 while eliciting a compensatory FGFR1 upregulation in apoptotic tubular cells.
papers.summary: In a unilateral aristolochic acid CKD model, the anti-fibrotic peptide AcSDKP given early (week 3) suppressed pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition, restored pericyte VEGF secretion and endothelial tubulogenesis, and improved renal function via the VEGF/FGFR1 axis, but in severely injured tubular cells it promoted apoptosis independently of FGFR1 by inhibiting AKT signaling, implying early, targeted dosing strategies.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 infection induces functional impairment of vitamin D receptor signaling to drive interleukin 6-dependent hyperinflammation in mononuclear phagocytes.
papers.summary: Integrating patient monocyte and dendritic cell transcriptomics with in vitro SARS-CoV-2-infected macrophage models, the authors show infection drives NF-kappaB-dependent IL-6 hyperproduction with upregulated IL6R-JAK-STAT3 signaling and simultaneous suppression of vitamin D receptor signaling and target genes. Calcitriol treatment suppressed IL-6 production, suggesting VDR restoration could temper COVID-19 hyperinflammation.

papers.title: A bioinformatic single-cell and structure-informed framework identifies a baicalin-CA2-keratinocyte state axis in atopic dermatitis.
papers.summary: Integrating pharmacogenomic target mining, machine-learning feature selection, single-cell perturbation analysis, and molecular docking, the authors nominate CA2 (carbonic anhydrase II) in keratinocytes as a convergent baicalin target in atopic dermatitis, with computationally supported baicalin-CA2 binding and disease-associated keratinocyte state programs in metabolism, junctions, and proliferative quiescence, framing a testable therapeutic axis.

papers.title: Vitamin D alleviates indoxyl sulfate-induced inflammatory and cholesterol dysregulation in macrophages: Implications for vascular health in patients receiving hemodialysis.
papers.summary: In macrophages exposed to the uremic toxin indoxyl sulfate, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 pretreatment reduced proinflammatory M1 markers (iNOS, IL-6, IL-1beta), increased M2 markers (CD163, IL-10), preserved cholesterol efflux via time- and transporter-dependent modulation of ABCA1/ABCG1, and reduced intracellular lipid accumulation, suggesting vitamin D may protect vascular health in hemodialysis patients.

papers.title: Integrative network analysis identifies candidate genes shared between ferroptosis and cuproptosis pathways in rheumatoid arthritis pathogenesis.
papers.summary: Using WGCNA and differential expression on CD14+ monocyte RNA-seq from rheumatoid arthritis patients and controls, the authors identify FTH1, SOD2, and CDKN2A as shared hub genes of ferroptosis and cuproptosis pathways, associated with oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered metal homeostasis, and proinflammatory immune infiltration, and expressed predominantly in synovial macrophages and fibroblasts.

papers.title: Sustained hypoxia induces divergent response patterns in cardiac metabolic-immune adaptation and circadian rhythm regulation.
papers.summary: Comparative transcriptomics across sustained, prenatal, and adult subacute hypoxia shows divergent cardiac responses: sustained hypoxia induced 181 differentially expressed genes with distinct circadian gene changes and remodeling of the circadian interactome, with ASS1 as the predominant co-expression hub. Metabolic-immune pathways were strongly enriched versus circadian ones, nominating potential targets for chronic hypoxia-associated cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Can tiered open-source mandates optimize innovation? A differential game study osn platform vs. independent project dynamics in foundation software ecosystems.
papers.summary: A tripartite Stackelberg differential game model examines tiered open-source mandates in AI foundation software ecosystems. Tiered mandates outperform uniform ones when ecosystem heterogeneity exceeds thresholds, optimally imposing stricter compliance on platforms (0.60-0.75) than independents (0.25-0.40), with modeled ecosystem-health improvements of 15-40% under high compliance-cost asymmetry, formalizing differentiated mandates as policy levers.

papers.title: From gut to pancreas: Shared genetic susceptibility and biological convergence in acute pancreatitis and Crohn's disease.
papers.summary: Cross-trait GWAS analysis of acute pancreatitis and Crohn's disease shows significant positive genetic correlation, 86 shared SNPs, and six genome-wide pleiotropic loci with suggestive colocalization at 6q22.33. Eight prioritized genes (including RSPO3, ATG16L1, SMAD3, FADS1/2, PRKAA1, IRGM) converge on IL-23/Th17 signaling, autophagy, and lipid metabolism, explaining their comorbidity from shared genetic susceptibility.

papers.title: Remote periosteal distraction promotes ischemic diabetic foot wound repair associated with VEGF/VEGFR2-related angiogenic responses.
papers.summary: In a rabbit ischemic diabetic foot wound model, osteotomy-free remote periosteal distraction (RPD) for 7 days improved wound closure, epithelial thickness, and collagen deposition versus sham and controls. RPD increased serum VEGF, wound VEGF mRNA, CD31/VEGF/VEGFR2-positive areas, and micro-CT-measured vascular volume, suggesting a less invasive alternative to tibial distraction via VEGF/VEGFR2-driven angiogenesis.

papers.title: Immunometabolic crosstalk in gallstone disease: driving roles of bacterial infection, NETs and MMP activation.
papers.summary: This review integrates evidence that bacterial infection, neutrophil extracellular traps, and matrix metalloproteinase activation cooperate in gallstone disease: biliary colonization triggers cytokine release, oxidative stress, and MMP-mediated matrix and mucin barrier disruption that promotes cholesterol crystal nucleation, while NETs scaffold crystal aggregation; bile acid toxicity and lipid imbalance reinforce a pro-lithogenic, immunometabolic microenvironment.

papers.title: Dysregulation of the TLR4/MYD88 Signaling Pathway in Egyptian Females with Breast Cancer: Implications for Tumor Progression.
papers.summary: In 71 Egyptian females with breast cancer versus 70 matched controls, TLR4 and MYD88 expression were significantly elevated and increased progressively across molecular subtypes. Both genes discriminated breast cancer from controls with high accuracy (AUC 0.966 and 0.900), supporting TLR4/MYD88 pathway dysregulation as associated with breast cancer presence and progression.

papers.title: DNA methylation biomarkers for early detection of ovarian cancer.
papers.summary: This review evaluates DNA methylation biomarkers for early ovarian cancer detection: single-gene markers (BRCA1, RASSF1A, OPCML, HOXA9, HIC1) show variable performance while multi-gene panels and machine-learning classifiers discriminate better. Limitations include retrospective designs, few stage I-II samples, and insufficient prospective validation; clinical translation requires minimal signatures, standardized cfDNA workflows, and longitudinal validation.

papers.title: Genomic signatures of host-range divergence in the generalist Beauveria bassiana and the specialist Beauveria brongniartii.
papers.summary: Comparative genomics of the generalist Beauveria bassiana and specialist B. brongniartii shows highly conserved genome architecture, CAZyme repertoires, and core infection machinery, but substantial variation in biosynthetic gene clusters, including remodeling of virulence-associated clusters and type I PKS expansion in the specialist, plus species-specific effector orthogroups, associating host-range divergence with secondary metabolism and effectors.

papers.title: Genomic and Structural Analysis of Gamete Recognition Proteins in a Broadcast Spawning Echinoderm Mesocentrotus franciscanus.
papers.summary: Using a new de novo genome assembly for the sea urchin Mesocentrotus franciscanus, the authors resolve genomic structure and expression of gamete recognition proteins, including EBR1 with fewer tandem CUB-TSP1 repeats than previously described, highly expressed in female reproductive tissues. HSP110 shows broader expression, suggesting pleiotropy, and structural modeling proposes interaction hypotheses among EBR1, bindin, and HSP110.

papers.title: Positional Anchors and Cooperative Retained-Position Sets Define Non-Equivalent RNA Sequence Landscapes.
papers.summary: Exhaustively mutating three ribosome-inspired 20-nt RNA seeds shows foldability landscapes depend strongly on starting-sequence identity and individual nucleotide positions: single retained guanines act as positional anchors, combinations give super-additive foldability gains, and G-U wobble disabling preserves hierarchies. Local RNA sequence space is thus non-equivalent and shaped by position-specific and cooperative retained-position effects.

papers.title: Optimization of protoplast based DNA isolation and genome analysis in a gamma-irradiated Aspergillus niger mutant strain.
papers.summary: A protoplast-based DNA isolation protocol was optimized for a gamma-irradiated Aspergillus niger mutant, with yield maximized at 50 mg/mL enzyme and 0.8 M KCl. Illumina sequencing produced a 37.06 Mb draft genome (537 contigs, N50 363 kb, 48.2% GC, 97.95% BUSCO completeness), with annotation of glycolysis, TCA cycle, citrate biosynthesis genes, and diverse secondary metabolite biosynthetic gene clusters.

papers.title: Efficiency of griseofulvin and plumbagin in mitigating N-nitrosodiethylamine-induced hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.journal: Biotechnic & histochemistry : official publication of the Biological Stain Commission
papers.summary: In N-nitrosodiethylamine-induced hepatocellular carcinoma in mice, the natural compounds plumbagin (2 and 6 mg/kg intraperitoneal) and griseofulvin (225 and 450 mg/kg oral) dose-dependently restored liver enzymes, cholesterol, malondialdehyde, and antioxidant defenses, with histological improvement; high-dose plumbagin showed efficacy comparable to sorafenib, supporting further evaluation as complementary hepatoprotective agents.
